summary: I verified every claim below on the wire (DuckDB over Overture's public S3, DuckDB over the anonymous source.coop FSQ mirror, Overpass API, taginfo, Socrata APIs, and keyless Census bulk downloads). Headline: Overture Maps Places is the ONLY free source with a truck-specific repair category at scale — US-bbox `categories.primary='truck_repair'` = 10,858 rows in release 2026-07-22.0, with outstanding contact fill (phone 99.2%, website 70.3%, email 60.4%, socials 82.1%, ZIP 99.4%, mean confidence 0.840). Foursquare OS Places has ZERO truck-specific repair categories — its only repair leaf is "Automotive Repair Shop" (541,517 US) — but it DOES carry "Welding Service" (7,600) and "Machine Shop" (18,537) that the repo currently leaves unmapped. OSM is far thinner than the brief assumes: `shop=truck_repair` = 272 in the US (813 worldwide per taginfo), plus 431 `shop=car_repair` carrying `service:vehicle:truck_repair=yes` — roughly 700 shops total. Two tags named in the brief, `service:vehicle:truck` and `service:vehicle:hgv`, DO NOT EXIST (taginfo global count = 0); the real key is `service:vehicle:truck_repair` (1,381 global / 530 US). On licensing, the repo's existing ruling is correct and I found direct evidence for it: Overture's own docs state the Places theme "contains no OpenStreetMap data and carries none of the share-alike obligations", and the OSMF Collective Database Guideline's third worked example is almost verbatim this use case — complementing a proprietary POI list with OSM and de-duplicating "would not be covered by this guideline" and the proprietary data "may be subject to the ODbL share-alike terms". Critically, schema separation alone does NOT save you: the guideline says joining two databases by key for production performance "are equivalent to a reference" and that datasets "need not be physically separated to qualify as independent". Two urgent operational findings: (1) Overture has DEPRECATED `categories` and will REMOVE it in the September 2026 release in favour of `basic_category` + `taxonomy` — the repo's category_map.yaml maps `categories.primary` and will break; worse, `basic_category` collapses truck_repair and automotive_repair both into `automotive_service`, destroying the truck signal unless you migrate to `taxonomy`. (2) The S3 bucket now retains TWO releases (2026-06-17.0 and 2026-07-22.0), contradicting the pipeline docstring. No US federal registry of commercial vehicle repair facilities exists — FMCSA registers carriers, not shops — and Census NAICS confirms there is no truck-specific industry code ("Truck repair shops, general" indexes to 811111, which lumps cars and trucks at 84,101 US establishments). State licence registries exist but are per-state and uneven (NY publishes 54,563 geocoded DMV-licensed facilities; NJ publishes 1,167 with phone numbers). Ratings, reviews, photos and "truck brands supported" have NO free legal US source at all — Yelp's robots.txt explicitly prohibits automated access and Google Maps Platform forbids storing ratings, reviews, addresses or coordinates.

FIELD FILL for truck_repair (n=10,858): phone 10,773 (99.2%) · website 7,634 (70.3%) · email 6,562 (60.4%) · socials 8,915 (82.1%) · postcode 10,791 (99.4%) · street 10,809 (99.5%) · brand 568 (5.2%) · operating_status 6,671 (61.4%) · addresses[1].country='US' 9,795 (90.2%) · mean confidence 0.840 · confidence>=0.5 9,742 (89.7%). towing_service (21,870): phone 99.7%, website 75.4%, email 49.2%. trailer_repair (140): phone 100%, website 100%, email 1.
sources.caveats: (1) categories is DEPRECATED and will be REMOVED in the September 2026 release — the repo's data/config/category_map.yaml maps categories.primary and will break. basic_category is COARSER: truck_repair and automotive_repair BOTH map to 'automotive_service', so migrating to basic_category alone destroys the truck signal; taxonomy.primary/hierarchy must be used instead. The old-to-new mapping is published only as a Google Sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_i2S48zTDoHff0uX-d8Nes3bR-Xee8drx27Gyi80CQ0/edit) — not a stable machine-readable file. (2) The bucket now retains TWO releases (2026-06-17.0 and 2026-07-22.0); the pipeline docstring saying 'exactly one release' is stale. (3) NO opening_hours field exists — verified against the parquet schema. (4) My counts are bbox-based, so southern Canada / northern Mexico bleed in; the us_addr column shows 90.2% of truck_repair rows explicitly carry country='US'. (5) Overture's counts materially EXCEED Census establishment counts for the same activity (towing 21,870 vs CBP 488410 = 10,554; tires 55,001 vs CBP 441320 = 20,455), so expect duplicate/mobile/franchise-page listings — feed this into confidence, do not treat as ground truth. (6) Throughput from this network was ~2.7 MB/s single-stream; a full US category scan of the 6 relevant files took 247 s, the field-fill scan 423 s.

Also: ATP data is produced by scraping brand store-locator pages; the project's own position is that this output is CC0, but a cautious owner may want to read docs/WHY_SPIDER.md before depending on it. MEASURED 2022 US establishment counts: NAICS 811111 General Automotive Repair 84,101 est / 385,539 emp · 811121 Automotive Body, Paint & Interior Repair 34,665 · 811191 Automotive Oil Change & Lubrication 8,694 · 811198 All Other Automotive Repair 5,091 · 811310 Commercial & Industrial Machinery Repair 22,433 · 441320 Tire Dealers 20,455 · 423120 Motor Vehicle Supplies & New Parts Wholesalers 12,377 · 423130 Tire & Tube Wholesalers 2,527 · 488410 Motor Vehicle Towing 10,554 · 484121 General Freight Trucking Long-Distance TL 63,315. sources.name: US Census Bureau — 2022 NAICS Index File
sources.license: US Government work — public domain
sources.why_it_matters: Settles the classification question authoritatively. VERBATIM index entries: 811111 'Truck repair shops, general' · 811111 'Mobile automotive and truck repair services' · 488410 'Tow truck services' · 811121 'Truck trailer body shops' and 'Truck trailer paint and body repair' · 811198 'Automotive tire repair (except retreading) shops' · 811310 'Truck refrigeration repair and maintenance services' and 'Industrial truck (e.g., forklifts) repair and maintenance services'. sources.name: Census TIGER/Line — Primary and Secondary Roads (route base geometry)
sources.license: US Government work — PUBLIC DOMAIN. No attribution, no share-alike.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the licence-safe foundation for the routes table that does not yet exist. Because the requested output joins routes to shops and publishes the result, the ROUTE layer's licence propagates into that output. TIGER is public domain; OSM highways and Overture's Transportation theme are BOTH ODbL. Choosing TIGER (or FHWA NHPN / BTS NTAD National Highway System, both also federal public domain) keeps the entire route-to-shop product free of share-alike.
sources.caveats: TIGER geometry is cartographic, not routing-grade — it is not a connected, turn-restricted network. If the owner needs true network distance rather than straight-line buffer distance, that needs a routable graph, and the free routable graphs (OSM/Valhalla/OSRM) are ODbL. [UNVERIFIED] whether FHWA NHPN bulk download is currently live — https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/planning/processes/tools/nhpn/ returns 200 but I did not test the download itself; the BTS geodata API call I tried returned 400.

sources.why_it_matters: VERBATIM, the clauses that decide the repo's question. §1.0: '"Collective Database" – Means this Database in unmodified form as part of a collection of independent databases in themselves that together are assembled into a collective whole. A work that constitutes a Collective Database will not be considered a Derivative Database.' and '"Derivative Database" – Means a database based upon the Database, and includes any translation, adaptation, arrangement, modification, or any other alteration of the Database or of a Substantial part of the Contents. This includes, but is not limited to, Extracting or Re-utilising the whole or a Substantial part of the Contents in a new Database.' §4.4(b): 'For the avoidance of doubt, Extraction or Re-utilisation of the whole or a Substantial part of the Contents into a new database is a Derivative Database and must comply with Section 4.4.' §4.5: 'a. ...You are not required to license Collective Databases under this License if You incorporate this Database or a Derivative Database in the collection, but this License still applies to this Database or a Derivative Database as a part of the Collective Database; b. Using this Database, a Derivative Database, or this Database as part of a Collective Database to create a Produced Work does not create a Derivative Database for purposes of Section 4.4; and c. Use of a Derivative Database internally within an organisation is not to the public and therefore does not fall under the requirements of Section 4.4.' §4.6 requires offering recipients 'a copy in a machine readable form of: a. The entire Derivative Database; or b. A file containing all of the alterations made to the Database or the method of making the alterations'.
sources.caveats: §4.5(c) is the biggest lever available to this project and is easy to miss: internal-only use of a Derivative Database does NOT trigger share-alike at all. The whole analysis changes depending on whether the platform is publicly served.

sources.name: OSMF Community Guideline — Collective Database
sources.owner: OpenStreetMap Foundation (endorsed by the OSMF board 2016-06-17)
sources.license: Page content CC-BY-SA 2.0
sources.why_it_matters: THE decisive document, quoted verbatim. The rule: 'An OSM dataset and a non-OSM dataset combined in a single database will be considered independent (and thus form a Collective Database rather than a Derivative Database) so long as the data used for a particular data type is either all OSM or all non-OSM within the same regional cut.' The four safe patterns are: 'the non-OSM and OSM datasets do not reference each other; or non-OSM data completely replaces a particular type of geometry or data for a primary feature within a regional cut ...; or the non-OSM data adds a particular type of geometry or data for a primary feature that was not already present within a regional cut ...; or a non-OSM database replaces or adds a property of a primary feature, and uses either all OSM data or no OSM data for that property ... ; or a combination of the above.' The two clauses that kill the 'separate schema' defence: 'Technical implementations that are functionally equivalent to a reference but facilitate performance improvements -- for example joining two databases together by a key for purposes of a production database -- are equivalent to a reference.' and 'Two data sets need not be physically separated to qualify as "independent" for purposes of the definition of a Collective Database.' And the worked example that IS this exact use case: 'You have a proprietary list of restaurants for a country. You would like to complement your list with the corresponding data from OpenStreetMap removing any duplicate objects in the process. The resulting, combined database would not be covered by this guideline and you would, if the dataset is publicly used, have to consider that your proprietary data may be subject to the ODbL share-alike terms.'
sources.caveats: Community guidelines are the OSMF's stated interpretation, not binding law, and this one is from 2016. It also says explicitly: 'This does not imply ... that the situations described are the only ways in which data can be combined without invoking share-alike, just that these are approaches we consider to be in line with the goals of the project.'

sources.name: OSMF Community Guideline — Horizontal Map Layers
sources.license: Page content CC-BY-SA 2.0
sources.why_it_matters: Reinforces the same test in map-layer terms: if 'all data for that Feature Type is from non-OpenStreetMap sources, then the ODbL share-alike conditions do not apply to that Feature Type', but if 'you use OpenStreetMap data along with non-OpenStreetMap data for a given Feature Type, then the share-alike condition would apply'. Its restaurant example maps 1:1 onto truck-repair POIs: 'restaurants added in your non-OpenStreetMap layer must be shared' when OSM and non-OSM restaurant data coexist.
sources.caveats: Framed around rendered maps; the Collective Database guideline is the more directly applicable one for a database.

sources.name: OSMF Community Guideline — Geocoding
sources.license: Page content CC-BY-SA 2.0
sources.why_it_matters: Defines the one NARROW path where OSM lookups can touch permissive data without share-alike: individual results 'may be stored and used together with other proprietary or third party data without having a share-alike impact', because a Direct Hit contains 'an insubstantial amount of raw OSM data'. But it closes the door on the bulk case: 'If Geocoding Results are used to create a new database that contains the whole or a substantial part of the contents of the OSM database, this new database would be considered a Derivative Database.' So: enriching ONE API response with ONE OSM lookup is defensible; bulk-joining ~700 OSM truck shops into a published table is not.
sources.caveats: Written for address geocoding, not POI enrichment. Relying on it for POI joins is an analogy, not a direct fit — do not treat it as a green light.

sources.name: Yelp — ratings, review counts, review text, photos
sources.license: Proprietary; all rights reserved
sources.why_it_matters: Definitively closes off the requested rating / review count / review summary / photos fields from Yelp. Yelp's robots.txt states verbatim: 'Use of any robot, spider, service search/retrieval application, or other automated device, process or means to access, retrieve, copy, scrape, or index any portion of the service or any content is prohibited, except as expressly permitted by Yelp.'
sources.caveats: The Yelp Fusion API exists with a free tier, but it is an API key plus display-and-caching restrictions, and its content may not be stored as a durable dataset. Out of scope under the project's constraints.

sources.name: Google Maps Platform — Places data (ratings, reviews, Place IDs, coordinates)
sources.license: Proprietary, paid API
sources.why_it_matters: Settles the 'Google Maps URL' field. Per the Maps Service Terms: Place IDs may be cached; ratings, reviews, addresses and latitude/longitude may NOT be stored; other cached Place data expires after 30 days; and Google Maps Content may not be used with a non-Google map. So the platform can neither store Google ratings nor hold a durable Google identifier without the paid Places API.
sources.caveats: A plain deep link the platform CONSTRUCTS from its own coordinates — https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={lat},{lon} — contains no Google data and is just a hyperlink; that is the legal way to satisfy 'Google Maps URL'. It must be generated at render time from our own lat/lon, never stored as data sourced from Google.

sources.name: California Bureau of Automotive Repair / DCA Open Data Portal
sources.license: State of California open data; terms not enumerated on the page
sources.why_it_matters: Worth reporting as a NEGATIVE result, because CA legally requires every automotive repair dealer to hold an ARD licence and so looks like the ideal registry. It is not published as bulk open data: the portal offers only aggregate statistics (License Population by County, Annual Licensing Statistics, enforcement measures), not the per-licensee list. The full list would require a California Public Records Act request.
sources.caveats: Only individual lookups are available via search.dca.ca.gov, which is a per-record UI, not a bulk source. Do not build a scraper against it.

sources.name: FMCSA / USDOT data portals — checked, NO repair-facility registry exists
sources.license: US Government work — public domain
sources.http_status: 200 (catalog searched; mobile.fmcsa.dot.gov QCDevsite returned 403 to automated fetch)
sources.approx_rows: 21 catalog matches for 'repair', all Takata airbag recall assets — zero repair-facility registries
sources.why_it_matters: Important negative finding, verified rather than assumed. FMCSA registers MOTOR CARRIERS (MC/DOT numbers) and publishes roadside inspection and violation data; it does not register or publish repair facilities. There is no federal equivalent of a 'DOT-approved truck repair shop' list. Anyone claiming otherwise is wrong.
sources.caveats: FMCSA's Vehicle Inspections and Violations dataset (876r-jsdb) is inspections OF carriers, not repair shops. The FMCSA QCMobile API docs endpoint returned 403 to my user-agent — [UNVERIFIED] whether it exposes anything relevant, but based on the documented scope it does not.

recommendations: ADOPT Overture `truck_repair` (10,858 US) + `trailer_repair` (140) as the truck-specific spine. It is the only free source with a truck-specific repair category at scale, and its contact fill is exceptional: phone 99.2%, website 70.3%, email 60.4%, socials 82.1%, ZIP 99.4%, mean confidence 0.840. FSQ contributes ZERO truck-specificity; OSM contributes ~700 shops total. Everything else is corroboration.

URGENT — Overture DEPRECATED `categories` and will REMOVE it in the SEPTEMBER 2026 release. data/config/category_map.yaml maps `categories.primary` and will break in ~2 months. Do NOT migrate to `basic_category`: it is coarser and collapses BOTH truck_repair and automotive_repair into `automotive_service`, destroying exactly the signal this project needs. Migrate to `taxonomy.primary` / `taxonomy.hierarchy`. Observed old->new basic_category pairs from this run: truck_repair->automotive_service, trailer_repair->automotive_service, towing_service->vehicle_service, roadside_assistance->vehicle_service, emergency_roadside_service->automotive_service, tire_dealer_and_repair->automotive_service, welders->building_or_construction_service, truck_dealer->vehicle_dealer, truck_stop->ground_transport_facility_or_service, truck_gas_station->gas_station, b2b_truck_equipment_parts_and_accessories->b2b_transportation_and_storage_service.

ADD the missing truck-relevant categories to category_map.yaml. FSQ: 'Business and Professional Services > Welding Service' (7,600 US) and 'Business and Professional Services > Machine Shop' (18,537 US) are unmapped and directly serve the requested `welding` field. Overture: `welders` (1,315) and `welding_supply_store` (2,366) are likewise unmapped. Overture `trailer_dealer` (6,307) and `truck_rentals` (40,428) may also be worth honest general slugs.

KEEP the present_in CHECK constraint and the osm.*-only ruling — the evidence supports it, and I now have the citation. The OSMF Collective Database Guideline's third worked example is this exact scenario (complement a proprietary POI list with OSM, de-duplicating) and says the result 'would not be covered by this guideline' and the proprietary data 'may be subject to the ODbL share-alike terms'. Crucially, physical schema separation is NOT a defence: the same guideline says joining two databases by key for production performance is 'equivalent to a reference', and datasets 'need not be physically separated to qualify as independent'. What makes a design safe is FEATURE-TYPE PURITY within a regional cut, not table naming.

IF the platform is INTERNAL-ONLY today, re-open the whole OSM decision. ODbL §4.5(c) is explicit: 'Use of a Derivative Database internally within an organisation is not to the public and therefore does not fall under the requirements of Section 4.4.' The share-alike trigger is Public Use. This is the single biggest lever available and it costs nothing to decide deliberately rather than by default.

THREE licence-safe ways to use OSM truck data even when publishing: (a) FEATURE-TYPE PURITY — use OSM as the SOLE source for feature types where no permissive data is mixed in for that region (weigh stations, highway junctions, rest areas already work this way in osm.*); (b) PRODUCED WORK — §4.5(b) says using the database to create a Produced Work does not create a Derivative Database, so rendering OSM shops on a map or in human-readable prose is fine where a bulk joined table is not; (c) SEPARATE ODbL LAYER — publish an explicitly ODbL-licensed, attributed 'also seen in OpenStreetMap' layer that is never merged or de-duplicated into the core answer.

ROUTE BASE GEOMETRY IS A LICENCE DECISION, and it must be made before the routes table is created. The route<->shop join output inherits the route layer's licence. Census TIGER/Line PRISECROADS and the federal NHPN/NTAD National Highway System are PUBLIC DOMAIN. OSM highways AND Overture's Transportation theme are BOTH ODbL — Overture's own attribution page shows 'Transportation — License for theme: ODbL' while Places carries no such line. Building routes on Overture Transportation would silently re-import the exact share-alike problem the businesses ruling avoids.

ADD AllThePlaces (CC0-1.0) as a third permissive source. It is the ONLY free source in this study carrying per-location `opening_hours`, `image` (photo URL) and `email` — three requested fields that Overture and FSQ structurally cannot fill (both schemas verified: no hours, no photos). Truck-relevant US spiders confirmed present include fleetpride_us, loves_us, pilot_flying_j, commercial_tire_us, goodyear_us, discount_tire, belle_tire_us, sullivan_tire_and_auto_service_us. CC0 means no attribution obligation and no share-alike, so it merges into core.businesses cleanly. Expect overlap with Overture (ATP already feeds it) — dedupe on nsi_id / brand:wikidata.

SET AN HONEST HOURS EXPECTATION AND ENCODE IT. Measured OSM fill: opening_hours on 16.2% of shop=truck_repair and 16.1% of shop=car_repair. Overture and FSQ have no hours at all. So national hours coverage will land well under 20%, concentrated in chains. `open_24x7` must be a tri-state (true / false / NULL=unknown) and NULL must render as 'unknown', never 'no' — the repo's own honesty rule already demands this.

USE CENSUS CBP AS A PUBLISHED COVERAGE DENOMINATOR. cbp22co.zip and zbp22detail.zip are keyless, public-domain, per-county and per-ZIP establishment counts by NAICS. Publishing 'we list N of the ~M establishments Census counts in NAICS 811111 in this county' would be a genuinely differentiating honesty feature and is cheap to build. Caveat it correctly: NAICS 811111 (84,101 US establishments) includes 'Truck repair shops, general' but lumps them with car repair, so it is an upper bound on trucks, not a truck count.

US FIELD MAPPING for the India-vocabulary fields: District -> COUNTY (assign by point-in-polygon against Census TIGER county polygons, public domain — NOT by a commercial geocoder). PIN Code -> ZIP (take `postcode` directly from Overture/FSQ, 99.4% filled on truck_repair; use Census ZCTA only when a polygon is needed, and label it ZCTA not ZIP, because USPS ZIPs are delivery routes and not areas). WhatsApp Number -> drop or hold permanently NULL: US commercial shops effectively do not publish WhatsApp business numbers, OSM's contact:whatsapp usage is negligible, and inventing one from `phone` would be fabrication.

GOOGLE MAPS URL: generate, never store. Emit https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={lat},{lon} at render time from OUR OWN coordinates. That is a hyperlink containing no Google data. Do not store Google Place IDs (paid Places API), and do not store Google ratings, reviews, addresses or coordinates — the Maps Service Terms forbid all four, and forbid using Google Maps Content with a non-Google map.

TREAT STATE LICENCE REGISTRIES AS THE VERIFICATION LAYER, NOT A DISCOVERY LAYER. There is NO federal repair-facility registry (verified: FMCSA registers carriers, not shops; a data.transportation.gov search for 'repair' returns only Takata recall assets). But NY publishes 54,563 geocoded DMV-licensed facilities with licence numbers and expiry dates, and NJ publishes 1,167 with phone numbers. A claim like 'holds a currently-valid NYS DMV repair-shop registration, expires 2028-03-31' is a real, defensible answer to the requested `verification status` / `last verified date` fields — far better than an invented score. Start with NY and NJ; treat wider state coverage as incremental, per-state work.

FIX THE STALE RELEASE COMMENT in scripts/businesses_pipeline.py. The docstring and category_map.yaml both assert the S3 bucket retains 'exactly one release, 2026-06-17.0'. As of today the listing shows TWO: release/2026-06-17.0/ and release/2026-07-22.0/. The discovery function takes max() so it will behave correctly, but the comment is now false and the repo's honesty rules apply to comments too.

OPTIMISE THE OVERTURE PULL WITH ROW-GROUP PRUNING. The 2026-07-22.0 places release is 74,223,561 rows across 16 parquet files (~11.2 GB), but only SIX files (parts 00000, 00001, 00002, 00003, 00005, 00006) contain any CONUS row groups, holding 16,995,025 candidate rows (22.9%). Selecting those files by reading bbox row-group statistics via parquet_metadata() first — a footer-only read — cut my full US category scan to 247 s and the field-fill scan to 423 s on a ~2.7 MB/s link. The current glob reads all 16.

CORRECT THE OSM TAG SET IN ANY SPEC OR CODE. `service:vehicle:truck` and `service:vehicle:hgv` DO NOT EXIST (taginfo global total = 0 for both). The correct US tags, with measured US counts: shop=truck_repair 272 · service:vehicle:truck_repair (any value) 530, of which shop=car_repair + service:vehicle:truck_repair=yes 431 · service:vehicle:towing 304 · service:vehicle:tyres 1,221 · shop=tyres 7,401 · shop=trailer 96 · shop=truck_parts 6 · amenity=vehicle_inspection 484 · craft=metal_construction 1,155 · craft=blacksmith 127. amenity=truck_repair does not exist (0).

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Truck brands supported (Volvo / Freightliner / Peterbilt / Kenworth / Mack / International authorized service)
unfillable_or_risky.problem: No free legal bulk source exists. Each OEM publishes an authorised-dealer locator on its own website under its own ToS; there is no open dataset of 'brands this shop is certified to service'. Overture's `brand` field means the shop's OWN brand (e.g. 'Rush Truck Centers'), not brands serviced, and it is only 5.2% filled on truck_repair (568 of 10,858).
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Three honest layers, all marked as inference, never as fact: (1) Overture `brand.names.primary` + `brand.wikidata` and OSM `brand:wikidata` — reliable for chain identity only; (2) AllThePlaces `brand` / `brand:wikidata` / `nsi_id` (CC0) for chain locations; (3) a deterministic name-token match against a curated brand list held in git with an evidence_url per entry — exactly the pattern the repo already uses for data/config/def_brands.yaml — writing brands_supported='inferred' and leaving it NULL otherwise. Never assert OEM certification the platform cannot evidence.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Average rating, review count, review summary
unfillable_or_risky.problem: No free legal US source at any scale. Yelp's robots.txt explicitly prohibits automated access to any portion of its content. Google Maps Platform forbids storing ratings and reviews (Place IDs only, 30-day cache on everything else, and no use with a non-Google map). Overture, FSQ, OSM and every government registry examined carry no ratings whatsoever.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Leave the fields permanently NULL (= unknown) rather than fabricating. If a quality signal is genuinely needed, compute an INTERNAL corroboration score from independent open evidence — how many permissive sources list the POI, whether a current state licence exists, Overture per-record confidence (mean 0.840 on truck_repair), and observed_at recency — and label it unambiguously in the UI as a data-corroboration score, NOT a customer rating. Conflating the two would be the single most misleading thing this platform could do.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: No free legal source of business photos. Google and Yelp photos are prohibited. Wikimedia Commons has essentially no coverage of US truck repair shops. Mapillary is street-level imagery of the ROAD (not the business), requires a free token, and is CC-BY-SA — share-alike, which reintroduces exactly the licence problem the project is trying to avoid on the core table.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: AllThePlaces `image` (CC0-1.0) — a per-location image URL where the chain's own store locator publishes one. Chains only; independents will be empty. Store the URL, not the bytes, and leave NULL for everything else. Do not add Mapillary to a permissively-licensed table.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: Structurally poor coverage, and the two best POI sources cannot help at all. I verified both parquet schemas directly: Overture Places has NO opening_hours field, and FSQ OS Places has NO hours field. The only free sources are OSM `opening_hours` — measured at 16.2% fill on US shop=truck_repair (44 of 272) and 16.1% on shop=car_repair (7,604 of 47,290), with only 149 US car_repair objects tagged opening_hours=24/7 — and AllThePlaces (chains only).
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Union of OSM `opening_hours` and AllThePlaces `opening_hours` (CC0), with the OSM contribution kept in the osm.* schema and surfaced as a separate ODbL-attributed layer rather than merged. Model open_24x7 as tri-state true/false/NULL and render NULL as 'unknown'. Plan the product around <20% national hours coverage — do not promise it.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: Vocabulary imported from an India-market spec; it does not transfer. US commercial vehicle repair businesses effectively do not publish WhatsApp business numbers, OSM's `contact:whatsapp` usage is negligible, and no US dataset examined carries the field. Deriving it by assuming the landline is on WhatsApp would be fabrication.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Drop the field for the US product, or keep it permanently NULL='unknown'. If a messaging channel is genuinely wanted, the honest US equivalents that DO exist are FSQ's facebook_id / instagram / twitter and Overture's `socials[]` — filled on 82.1% of Overture truck_repair rows (8,915 of 10,858).

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Mobile service · roadside breakdown · towing · welding · spare parts · tyre repair · battery service (as per-shop boolean capability flags)
unfillable_or_risky.problem: These are CATEGORY memberships in the open data, not per-shop capability flags. A shop categorised `truck_repair` carries no machine-readable statement of whether it does welding or battery work. OSM's service:vehicle:* namespace is the only true capability vocabulary and it is far too thin in the US to be a national answer: service:vehicle:truck_repair 530, service:vehicle:towing 304, service:vehicle:tyres 1,221, and service:vehicle:batteries only 3,225 WORLDWIDE.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Derive each flag ONLY from an explicit category and mark it as such, leaving NULL when no category applies: towing <- Overture towing_service (21,870) / FSQ 'Towing Service' (9,650); roadside/mobile <- Overture roadside_assistance (1,277) + emergency_roadside_service (655) + mobile_dent_repair (6); welding <- Overture welders (1,315) + welding_supply_store (2,366) / FSQ 'Welding Service' (7,600) + 'Machine Shop' (18,537); tyre repair <- Overture tire_dealer_and_repair (42,817) + tire_shop (12,184) + tire_repair_shop (748) / FSQ 'Tire Repair Shop' (23,753); spare parts <- Overture automotive_parts_and_accessories (52,802) + b2b_truck_equipment_parts_and_accessories (918). Battery service has NO usable US source — leave NULL. Do not infer capabilities from shop names.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Google Maps URL (as a stored data field)
unfillable_or_risky.problem: Storing a Google identifier requires the paid Places API, and the Maps Service Terms permit caching Place IDs only — ratings, reviews, addresses and lat/lng may not be stored, other Place data expires after 30 days, and Google Maps Content may not be used with a non-Google map.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Do not store anything from Google. GENERATE the link at render time from the platform's own coordinates: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={lat},{lon}. That is a hyperlink to a public website containing zero Google-sourced data, and it satisfies the user need without touching the Places API.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: No free source is close to complete for TRUCK-SPECIFIC repair. Measured ceilings: Overture 10,858 truck_repair + 140 trailer_repair; OSM ~700 (272 shop=truck_repair + 431 car_repair tagged with truck repair service, overlap unmeasured); FSQ literally zero. Against that, Census CBP 2022 counts 84,101 establishments in NAICS 811111, and the Census NAICS index confirms 'Truck repair shops, general' and 'Mobile automotive and truck repair services' both classify there — meaning no free source can even tell you how many US truck repair shops exist, let alone list them. Separately, Overture materially OVER-counts against Census for comparable activities (towing 21,870 vs CBP 488410 = 10,554; tyre retail 55,001 vs CBP 441320 = 20,455), so its raw counts are not a headcount either.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: State the ceiling openly and design around it. Realistic union after conflation is on the order of 11,000-12,000 TRUCK-LABELLED shops nationally. If general repair is also surfaced (Overture automotive_repair 201,199 / FSQ 'Automotive Repair Shop' 541,517), physical coverage of 'a shop a stranded tractor could use' becomes high, but truck-specificity is weak — which is precisely why the repo's existing decision to map those to an honest `auto_repair` slug rather than relabel them `truck_repair` is correct and should not be softened. Publish per-county coverage against CBP so the gap is visible rather than implied.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Distance from route · route id(s) · route name(s) · nearest route point · nearest highway junction · travel direction
unfillable_or_risky.problem: Not a data-source problem — there is no routes table anywhere in the schema, so none of these can be computed today. And the choice of route geometry is a licence decision that propagates into every published row of the join: OSM highways and Overture Transportation are both ODbL, so a published route<->shop table built on either becomes a Derivative Database.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Build the route layer on PUBLIC-DOMAIN federal geometry — Census TIGER/Line PRISECROADS (verified live) or FHWA NHPN / BTS NTAD National Highway System. Use straight-line (geography ST_DWithin) buffer distance for the 2-5 km requirement, which TIGER supports fine. Nearest highway junction from TIGER/NHPN interchange features rather than OSM highway=motorway_junction. If true network distance is later required, note that every free routable graph (OSM/Valhalla/OSRM) is ODbL — though a computed scalar distance is arguably a Produced Work under ODbL §4.5(b), that is a call the owner should make explicitly, not by accident.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Verification status · confidence score · last verified date
unfillable_or_risky.problem: There is no external source for these; they are entirely internal computations, which makes them the easiest fields in the whole spec to accidentally fabricate.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Ground every one of them in something observable and cite it: verification_status from an actual state-licence match (NY DMV licence number + expiry date; NJ licence id) or from multi-source agreement, never as a bare label; confidence from the repo's existing quality.compute_confidence with Overture's own per-record confidence as an input (mean 0.840 on truck_repair, 89.7% at >=0.5); last_verified_date from the contributing source's observed_at — Overture release vintage or FSQ date_refreshed — and NEVER the download date, per the repo's own honesty rule.

open_questions: Is the platform PUBLICLY USED, or internal-only? ODbL §4.5(c) states outright that internal organisational use of a Derivative Database 'is not to the public and therefore does not fall under the requirements of Section 4.4'. If truck-intel is internal today, OSM's ~700 truck shops and its service:vehicle:* capability tags become usable with no share-alike consequence at all, and the osm.*-only ruling could be relaxed deliberately. This single answer changes the whole architecture and should be decided consciously rather than inherited.

Would the owner accept publishing a SEPARATE, explicitly ODbL-licensed 'OpenStreetMap truck-repair layer' alongside the permissive core? That would unlock OSM's opening_hours (the only per-shop hours in any keyless source) and its service:vehicle:* capability tags, at the cost of that one layer being share-alike. The alternative is the status quo: OSM stays query-time-only and those fields stay NULL.

Overture removes `categories` in the SEPTEMBER 2026 release. Migrate the pipeline to `taxonomy` now (correct but the new taxonomy has no published machine-readable file — only a Google Sheet), or pin to a retained release and defer? Note the bucket currently retains only two releases, so pinning has a short shelf life.

Does a free-registration API key fall inside or outside the project's 'no paid API keys' rule? It matters in three places: FSQ's current release is behind a gated-but-free Hugging Face token (the anonymous source.coop mirror is frozen at 2025-02-06, now ~17 months stale); the Census DATA API now returns 'Missing Key' (though the bulk CBP files I used are keyless); and SAM.gov's extract listing returns an empty array without an api.sam.gov key.

Should general `automotive_repair` be surfaced to truckers at all? It is 201,199 rows in Overture and 541,517 in FSQ — it will numerically dominate any result set and drown the 10,858 genuinely truck-specific shops. The existing category_map already maps it to an honest `auto_repair` slug, but the RANKING and default filtering decision is a product call I could not make for the owner.

What does 'within 2-5 km of the route' mean — straight-line or road-network distance? Straight-line works on public-domain TIGER geometry. Network distance requires a routable graph, and every free one is ODbL. This needs deciding before the routes table is designed, not after.

How many of Overture's 10,858 truck_repair rows survive the repo's existing 150 m / 0.85 conflation against FSQ? Because FSQ has NO truck category, every one of those merges will be against a general 'Automotive Repair Shop' record, so I expect the 0.55-0.85 'dedup_gray_zone' band to be unusually wide. I did not measure this — it needs a real conflation dry-run before anyone quotes a final national figure.

Is per-state licence-registry ingestion worth the effort beyond NY and NJ? Each state is a bespoke integration with a different schema, and CA — despite legally licensing every repair dealer — publishes only aggregate statistics and would need a Public Records Act request. The payoff is the `verification status` field, which nothing else can fill honestly.

I verified the EPA FRS national_combined.zip endpoint is live (HTTP 206 on a range request) but did NOT download or count it. How many facilities carry NAICS 8111xx with usable coordinates is unknown, and it is the most promising remaining federal source with names + addresses + lat/lon + NAICS. Worth a follow-up measurement before it is either adopted or dismissed.

The AllThePlaces bulk-download URL could not be verified — the builds page is JavaScript-rendered and the historical alltheplaces-data.openaddresses.io paths now 404/416. Someone needs to read the live URL off the page before a fetcher is written, and to skim docs/WHY_SPIDER.md so the owner is comfortable with the provenance of a CC0 dataset produced by scraping brand store-locator pages.
